docs.title: Welcome to Sonata 🎵
docs.text: Sonata is a Discord bot that brings RateYourMusic ratings and music discovery features to your Discord server. Connect with your community, share your favorite albums, and explore music tastes together!

docs.title: 📋 Features
docs.text:
• Retrieve information about music releases.
  • Check user profiles and statistics.
  • Explore ratings within your Discord server.

docs.title: 1. Set up Last.fm (Recommended)
docs.text:
Start by linking your Last.fm account to enable automatic track detection:

!setlastfm your_lastfm_username

This allows commands to automatically use the track you're currently listening to.

docs.title: 2. Import Your Ratings
docs.text:
Then, import your ratings from RateYourMusic:

  1. Go to RateYourMusic Export
  2. Click "Begin export..." and download your CSV file
  3. Use the import command with your CSV file attached:
!importratings

Warning

Depending on the number of ratings you have, the import process may take a while. Please be patient and do not try to re-run the command while the import is still in progress.

docs.title: 3. Explore Commands
docs.text: Now you're all set! Check out the available commands.

docs.title: 💡 Popular Commands
docs.text:
Here are some commands to get you started:

Command Description !profile View your rating statistics !release OK Computer Get information about an album !artistratings Radiohead See all your ratings for an artist !bestratedreleases View the server's top-rated albums !lyrics Get lyrics for your current track !samples Discover samples in your current track !aoty View best albums of the year

docs.title: 📖 Support & Links
docs.text:
• Setup Guide – Install and configure your own instance
  • GitHub Repository – Source code and issues
  • RateYourMusic – Where your ratings come from
  • Last.fm – Automatic track detection

Data privacy

All rating data is stored locally on the bot's instance. No data is shared with third parties beyond the API calls to fetch public music information.

docs.title: What is Sonata?
docs.text: Sonata is a Discord bot that integrates RateYourMusic ratings with your Discord server, allowing you to share, compare, and discover music with your community.

docs.title: Is Sonata free?
docs.text: Yes! Sonata is completely free and open-source. You can host your own instance or contribute to the project on GitHub.

docs.title: Do I need a RateYourMusic account?
docs.text: Yes, you need a RateYourMusic account to export your ratings. You can create one at rateyourmusic.com.

docs.title: Do I need a Last.fm account?
docs.text: No, but it's highly recommended! Last.fm integration allows Sonata to automatically detect what you're currently listening to, making many commands easier to use.

docs.title: How do I add Sonata to my server?
docs.text: If someone is hosting a public instance, they can provide you with an invite link. Otherwise, you'll need to host your own instance by following the Setup Guide.

docs.title: Where do I get the required API keys?
docs.text:
You'll need:

  • Discord Bot Token: Discord Developer Portal
  • Last.fm API Key: Last.fm API
  • Genius API Token: Genius API

See the Setup Guide for detailed instructions.

docs.title: How do I import my ratings?
docs.text:
1. Go to RateYourMusic Export
  2. Click "Begin export..." and download your CSV file
  3. Use the command !importratings with your CSV file attached

See the importratings command for more details.

docs.title: How long does the import take?
docs.text: Import time depends on the number of ratings you have. For a few hundred ratings, it should take less than a minute. For thousands of ratings, it may take several minutes. The bot will notify you when the import is complete.

docs.title: Will importing delete my existing ratings?
docs.text: Yes! Importing ratings will overwrite all your existing ratings in the bot. This ensures your data stays in sync with RateYourMusic.

docs.title: How do I link my Last.fm account?
docs.text:
Use the command:

!setlastfm your_lastfm_username

Replace your_lastfm_username with your actual Last.fm username.

docs.title: What's the difference between prefix commands and slash commands?
docs.text:
Sonata supports both:

  • Prefix commands (e.g., !release) – Traditional Discord commands using the ! prefix
  • Slash commands (e.g., /release) – Modern Discord commands with autocomplete

Most commands support both methods.

docs.title: Why isn't a command working?
docs.text:
Common reasons:

  1. Missing Last.fm setup: Some commands require Last.fm to be set up with !setlastfm
  2. No ratings imported: Many server statistics require at least some users to have imported ratings
  3. Insufficient permissions: Make sure the bot has proper permissions in the channel
  4. Typo in command: Double-check the command name and arguments

docs.title: Can I use commands without specifying a song?
docs.text: Yes! Many commands can automatically detect what you're currently listening to on Last.fm. You must first link your account with !setlastfm.

docs.title: How are "best rated" rankings calculated?
docs.text:
Best rated commands use a weighted formula that considers:

  • Average rating score
  • Number of ratings
  • Number of distinct releases (for artists)

This prevents albums/artists with only one or two highly-rated entries from dominating the rankings.

docs.title: Where is my data stored?
docs.text: All data is stored in a local SQLite database on the bot's host machine. Nothing is sent to external servers except for API calls to fetch public music information.

docs.title: Can other users see my ratings?
docs.text: Yes, once you import your ratings, other server members can see them through various commands like !whoratedrelease and !profile.

docs.title: Can I delete my data?
docs.text: Yes! You can delete all your ratings by importing an empty CSV file, or the bot owner can delete your data from the database.

docs.title: Does Sonata track my listening history?
docs.text: No. Sonata only fetches your currently playing track from Last.fm when you use commands that need it. No listening history is stored.

docs.title: The bot isn't responding to my commands
docs.text:
1. Check that the bot is online (green status indicator)
  2. Verify the bot has "Read Messages" and "Send Messages" permissions
  3. Try using the bot in a different channel
  4. Check if slash commands work: /profile

docs.title: "No Last.fm username set" error
docs.text:
You need to link your Last.fm account first:

!setlastfm your_lastfm_username

docs.title: "No ratings found" error
docs.text:
This means either:

  • You haven't imported your ratings yet (use !importratings)
  • No one in the server has ratings for the specified artist/release
  • The search query didn't match any results (try different keywords)

docs.title: Import failed
docs.text:
Common causes:

  1. Wrong file format: Make sure you're uploading the CSV file from RateYourMusic
  2. Corrupted file: Try exporting and downloading the file again
  3. Network issues: Check your internet connection

docs.title: Lyrics not found
docs.text:
1. Not all songs have lyrics available on Genius
  2. Make sure you're currently playing a song on Last.fm

docs.title: Can I rate albums directly in Discord?
docs.text: No, Sonata is designed to import and display ratings from RateYourMusic, not create new ones. You should rate albums on rateyourmusic.com and then re-import your ratings.

docs.title: Does the bot support other music databases?
docs.text: Currently, Sonata only supports RateYourMusic. Support for other platforms may be added in the future.

docs.title: Can I see ratings from outside my server?
docs.text: No, all server-wide commands (like !bestratedreleases) only show ratings from members of your current server.

docs.title: Is there a limit to how many ratings I can import?
docs.text: No! You can import as many ratings as you want from RateYourMusic.

docs.title: Can I use the bot in DMs?
docs.text: Yes! Most commands work in direct messages with the bot. Server-specific commands (like !bestratedreleases) require you to be in a server.

docs.title: How can I contribute?
docs.text:
Check out the GitHub repository to:

  • Report bugs
  • Suggest features
  • Submit pull requests
  • Improve documentation

docs.title: Can I host multiple instances?
docs.text: Yes! Each instance has its own database, so you can run multiple bots for different servers or communities.

docs.title: What's the tech stack?
docs.text:
• Language: Python 3.10+
  • Discord Library: discord.py
  • Database: SQLite with Peewee ORM
  • APIs: Last.fm, Genius, RateYourMusic (web scraping)

docs.title: Still Have Questions?
docs.text:
If your question isn't answered here:

  1. Check the Setup Guide for configuration help
  2. Browse the command documentation
  3. Open an issue on GitHub

docs.title: Setup & Configuration
docs.text: This guide will help you set up and run Sonata bot on your own Discord server.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
Before you begin, make sure you have:

  • Python 3.10+ installed on your system
  • A Discord Bot Token from the Discord Developer Portal
  • A Last.fm API key from Last.fm API
  • A Genius API token from Genius API

docs.title: 1. Clone the Repository
docs.text:
git clone https://github.com/hsc00/sonata-bot.git
cd sonata-bot

docs.title: 2. Install Dependencies
docs.text:
You can install dependencies using pip:

pip install -r requirements.txt

Or use the justfile:

just install

docs.title: 3. Configure Environment Variables
docs.text:
Create a .env file in the root directory with the following variables:

# Discord Bot Token (Required)
DISCORD_TOKEN=your_discord_bot_token_here

# Last.fm API Credentials (Required)
LASTFM_API_KEY=your_lastfm_api_key_here
LASTFM_API_SECRET=your_lastfm_api_secret_here

# Genius API Token (Required for lyrics and samples commands)
GENIUS_API_TOKEN=your_genius_token_here

# Database Configuration (Optional)
DATABASE_PATH=./sonata.db

docs.title: 4. Set Up the Database
docs.text:
The bot uses SQLite for storing ratings and user information. The database will be created automatically on first run, but you can initialize it manually:

just migrate

Or:

python -c "from bot.database.migrations import run_migrations; run_migrations()"

docs.title: Running the Bot
docs.text:
Once everything is configured, you can start the bot:

just run

Or:

python bot/bot.py

The bot should now be online and ready to use!

docs.title: Creating a Bot Application
docs.text:
1. Go to the Discord Developer Portal
  2. Click "New Application" and give it a name
  3. Navigate to the "Bot" section in the left sidebar
  4. Click "Add Bot"
  5. Under the "Token" section, click "Copy" to get your bot token
  6. Paste this token into your .env file as DISCORD_TOKEN

docs.title: Bot Permissions
docs.text:
The bot requires the following permissions:

  • Read Messages/View Channels
  • Send Messages
  • Embed Links
  • Attach Files
  • Read Message History
  • Use External Emojis
  • Add Reactions

Permission Integer: 397284600896

docs.title: Inviting the Bot to Your Server
docs.text:
1. In the Developer Portal, go to the "OAuth2" > "URL Generator" section
  2. Select the "bot" scope
  3. Select the permissions listed above
  4. Copy the generated URL and open it in your browser
  5. Select the server you want to add the bot to and click "Authorize"

docs.title: Getting a Last.fm API Key
docs.text:
1. Visit Last.fm API Account Creation
  2. Fill out the form with your application details
  3. You'll receive an API Key and Shared Secret
  4. Add both to your .env file

docs.title: Getting a Genius API Token
docs.text:
1. Visit Genius API Clients
  2. Click "New API Client"
  3. Fill out the form with your application details
  4. Once created, click "Generate Access Token"
  5. Copy the token and add it to your .env file

docs.title: Bot doesn't respond to commands
docs.text:
• Verify the bot has proper permissions in your server
  • Check that the DISCORD_TOKEN in your .env file is correct
  • Make sure the bot is online (check the console for any error messages)
  • Try syncing slash commands: !sync guild or !sync global

docs.title: Import ratings fails
docs.text:
• Ensure your CSV file is exported correctly from RateYourMusic
  • Check that the file format matches RYM's export format
  • Wait for the import to complete - large libraries can take several minutes

docs.title: Last.fm integration not working
docs.text:
• Verify your LASTFM_API_KEY and LASTFM_API_SECRET are correct
  • Make sure you've set your Last.fm username with !setlastfm
  • Check that your Last.fm profile is public

docs.title: Lyrics/Samples not found
docs.text:
• Ensure your GENIUS_API_TOKEN is valid
  • Not all tracks have lyrics or sample information available
  • Try using the full artist and track name

docs.title: Development
docs.text:
For development work, you can use the development setup:

just setup

This will install the package in editable mode with development dependencies.

docs.title: Running Tests
docs.text: just test

docs.title: Code Quality
docs.text:
Check code quality:

just check

Auto-fix linting issues:

just lint-fix

Format code:

just format

docs.title: Documentation
docs.text:
To build and serve the documentation locally:

just docs-serve

The documentation will be available at http://127.0.0.1:8000/.

docs.title: Support
docs.text:
If you encounter any issues or have questions:

  1. Check the GitHub Issues page
  2. Review the documentation thoroughly
  3. Make sure all API keys are configured correctly
  4. Check the console output for detailed error messages

docs.title: 🧑‍🎤 Artist Commands
docs.text: Explore artist ratings, discover top-rated artists, and view statistics about your favorite musicians.

docs.title: !artistratings (!ar)
docs.text:
View all ratings for a specific artist, organized by release year and score.

If no artist is provided, the bot automatically uses the artist you're currently listening to on Last.fm. Results include the average score across all ratings for that artist.

Options:

  • User (optional) – Select another user by mention or Discord user ID. If not provided, shows your own ratings.
  • Artist (optional) – The artist you want to search for. If not provided, uses your currently playing artist on Last.fm.

Usage Examples

!artistratings
!artistratings Radiohead
!ar @user Radiohead

Order of Arguments

If specifying a user, they must come before the artist name in your command.

Last.fm Required

You must have set your Last.fm username with !setlastfm to use this command without specifying an artist.

docs.title: !bestratedartists (!bra)
docs.text:
Discover the best rated artists ranked using a sophisticated weighted formula that considers:

  • Average rating score
  • Total number of ratings
  • Number of distinct releases

Scope:

  • No user specified: Shows the best rated artists across the entire server
  • User specified: Shows only that user's best rated artists

Only artists with more than 3 ratings are included to ensure meaningful results.

Usage Examples

!bestratedartists
!bra @user

Tip

This is perfect for discovering consensus favorites in your community!

docs.title: !mostratedartists (!mra)
docs.text:
See which artists have received the most ratings, sorted by total rating count.

Find out which artists are most popular and widely listened to in your server!

Scope:

  • No user specified: Shows the most rated artists across the entire server
  • User specified: Shows only that user's most rated artists

Usage Examples

!mostratedartists
!mra @user

docs.title: 💿 Release Commands
docs.text: Browse albums, discover highly-rated releases, and explore what your server community is listening to.

docs.title: !release (!r, !a, !album)
docs.text:
Shows detailed information about a specific release from RateYourMusic, including ratings, genres, release date, and more.

If no release name is provided, the bot will use the release you're currently listening to on Last.fm.

Options:

  • Name (optional) – The name of the release you want to search for. Defaults to your currently playing track on Last.fm.

Usage Examples

!release
!release OK Computer
!album Radiohead OK Computer

docs.title: !whoratedrelease (!wr, !wa)
docs.text:
Shows a list of server members who have rated a specific release, sorted by their rating scores.

The command displays the average rating and total number of ratings for the release within your server.

Options:

  • Name (optional) – The name of the release you want to search for. Defaults to your currently playing track on Last.fm.

Usage Examples

!whoratedrelease
!whoratedrelease OK Computer
!wr Radiohead In Rainbows

docs.title: !bestratedreleases (!brr, !brab)
docs.text:
Shows the top-rated releases among server members, ranked using a weighted formula that considers both average rating and number of ratings.

Only releases with more than 3 ratings are included to ensure meaningful results.

Usage Examples

!bestratedreleases
!brr

Tip

This is a great way to discover highly-regarded albums within your community!

docs.title: !mostratedreleases (!mrr, !mrab)
docs.text:
Shows the most-rated releases among server members, sorted by the number of ratings received.

Usage Examples

!mostratedreleases
!mrr

docs.title: !randomrating (!rdr)
docs.text:
Shows a random release rated by a server member, with an optional filter for high or low ratings.

Options:

  • Filter (optional) – Filter to apply to the random selection:
    • glaze – Only high ratings (3.0+ out of 5)
    • roast – Only low ratings (2.0 or lower)

Usage Examples

!randomrating
!randomrating glaze
!randomrating roast

docs.title: !newreleases (!nr)
docs.text:
Displays new releases of the current week from various artists.

This command fetches the latest releases from Sputnikmusic and shows information about them, including ratings if available on RateYourMusic.

Usage Examples

!newreleases
!nr

docs.title: !albumoftheyear (!aoty)
docs.text:
Shows the best-rated releases of a specific year for a user, sorted by rating score.

Discover personal or community favorites from any year!

Options:

  • Year (optional) – The year you want to search for. If not provided, the current year will be used.
  • User (optional) – The user whose ratings you want to check. If not provided, shows your own ratings.

Usage Examples

!albumoftheyear
!aoty 2025
!aoty 2025 @username

Info

Year must be between 1900 and the current year.

docs.title: 🎵 Track Commands
docs.text: Get lyrics and discover musical relationships through samples and interpolations.

docs.title: !lyrics (!lr)
docs.text:
Fetch and display the lyrics for the track you're currently listening to on Last.fm.

The lyrics are synced and displayed in an easy-to-read, paginated format perfect for singing along or understanding the words!

Requirements:

  • You must have set your Last.fm username using !setlastfm
  • You must be currently listening to a track on Last.fm (or have recently played one)

Usage Examples

!lyrics
!lr

Data Source

Lyrics are fetched from various sources and may not be available for all tracks.

docs.title: 👤 User Commands
docs.text: Manage your profile, import ratings, and view community statistics.

docs.title: !setlastfm
docs.text:
Link your Last.fm account to enable automatic track detection across many commands.

This allows the bot to automatically fetch what you're currently listening to.

Options:

  • Username – Your Last.fm username

Usage Examples

!setlastfm myusername

docs.title: !importratings (!i)
docs.text:
Import all your ratings from a CSV file exported from RateYourMusic.

This is the core feature that enables all rating-based functionality in Sonata.

How to get your CSV file:

  1. Go to RateYourMusic Export
  2. Click "Begin export..." and wait for the export to complete
  3. Download your CSV file
  4. Attach the file when running this command

To attach a file:

  • Drag and drop the file into Discord, then type the command
  • Or click the ➕ button → "Upload a file" → Select your CSV → Type the command

Usage Examples

!importratings (with CSV file attached)
!i (with CSV file attached)

Import Time

The import process may take a while depending on the number of ratings you have. Please be patient and do not try to re-run the command while the import is still in progress.

Data Overwrite

Importing ratings will overwrite any existing ratings you have in the bot. This ensures your data stays in sync with RateYourMusic.

docs.title: !profile
docs.text:
View detailed statistics about your (or another user's) music taste, including:

  • Average rating score
  • Total releases rated
  • Number of unique artists rated

Options:

  • User (optional) – Select another user by mention or Discord user ID. If not provided, shows your own profile.

Usage Examples

!profile
!profile @user

docs.title: !ratingsrank (!rr)
docs.text:
View a leaderboard of server members ranked by the number of ratings they have submitted.

Usage Examples

!ratingsrank
!rr
